fold.quote: Unlike bulky 3-wheel electric bikes, Triker folds down small for SUVs and apartment-living. Ideal for daily use or weekend adventures. ⟶ Effortless Power, Your Way

Let’s circle back to that folding feature I touched on earlier, because it deserves some honest talk. The Triker does fold, allowing you to bring the front half back toward the rear, which reduces the wheelbase by about 15 inches. That’s not nothing, and it can be the difference between fitting it into that last spot in your SUV or not.
A central hinge in the frame allows the Triker to fold when it’s not being ridden ⟶ The saddle and its adjustable backrest felt cushy and comfortable.

notes: Maker calls it 'Velotric Triker' (no '1'); src link was correct. Page shows $2,499.00 with no crossed-out price and 'Sold out' (not stated as discontinued). It's an electric trike. Maker default speed 12 mph (Standard Mode), adjustable 8-20 mph, Beginner Mode 8 mph; 'Class 1/2' with throttle -> Class 2. EBR's 'TOP SPEED: 28 MPH' contradicts its own text (20 mph max). Maker gives battery only as 48V 16.75Ah (=804 Wh); both reviews say 804 Wh. Frame folds via a central hinge (both reviews).
